result:
The fix is in place and everything passes.

**What I changed:** `PostController.update()` (`app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:88-97`) was reading the raw request body with `await this.request.json()` and writing it through `Post.forceUpdate()`, which bypasses both validation and the model's fillable allowlist — so any key the client sent (including `authorId` and `createdAt`) landed straight in the row. It now validates with `PostPayloadSchema` — the same schema `store()` uses, so an empty/oversized `title`, `excerpt`, or `body` is refused with a 422 and field errors before anything is written — and persists via `Post.update()`, which applies `Post.fillable = ['title', 'excerpt', 'body']`; `authorId` is deliberately absent from that list, so ownership stays whatever the post was created with no matter what the body carries. I also added `tests/PostUpdate.test.ts` covering the five behaviours from the report: an `authorId` in the body leaves the post with its original author, an invalid payload 422s with `errors.title.0` and leaves the row untouched, out-of-form fields like `createdAt` are not written, an ordinary author edit still redirects and saves, and a non-author still gets a 403. `bun run typecheck` is clean and `bun test` passes 7/7 (the stack traces in the output are the framework logging the deliberately-triggered 422/403 exceptions); `bunx guren check` reports 0 failures.
